# EvA backend API skill - installer

Save this file anywhere (Downloads is fine), then follow **one** of the two options below.
It installs the EvA backend standards into Claude Code so it writes C# our way from the start.

Contains 12 files, 49 KB compressed. Author: Manwar Meraj.

---

## Option 1 - let Claude do it (easiest)

Open Claude Code in any folder and paste this, with the real path to this file:

```
Install the EvA backend skill from C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\EvA-Backend-Skill-Installer.md
- do not read the base64 payload, just run the PowerShell block in that file.
```

## Option 2 - do it yourself

Open **Windows PowerShell**, set the path on the first line, then paste the whole block:

```powershell
$File = "C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\EvA-Backend-Skill-Installer.md"   # <-- edit this

$lines  = Get-Content $File
$start  = ($lines | Select-String -SimpleMatch 'PAYLOAD-BEGIN' | Select-Object -Last 1).LineNumber
$end    = ($lines | Select-String -SimpleMatch 'PAYLOAD-END'   | Select-Object -Last 1).LineNumber
$b64    = ($lines[$start..($end - 2)]) -join ""

$zip    = Join-Path $env:TEMP "eva-skill.zip"
[IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($zip, [Convert]::FromBase64String($b64))

$target = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\skills\eva-backend-api-skill"
if (Test-Path $target) {
    $n = 1; while (Test-Path "$target.bak-$n") { $n++ }
    Move-Item $target "$target.bak-$n"
    Write-Host "Backed up your previous copy to $target.bak-$n"
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $target -Force | Out-Null
Expand-Archive -Path $zip -DestinationPath $target -Force
Remove-Item $zip -Force

Write-Host "Installed to $target" -ForegroundColor Green
Get-ChildItem $target -Recurse -File | Measure-Object | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.Count) files" }
```

---

## Check it worked

Start a **new** Claude Code session inside any EvA API repo and type `/skills`.
`eva-backend-api-skill` should be listed.

You never invoke it by name - it loads by itself whenever you touch C# in an
`eva-*-api` or `EVA.*.API` repo. Ask it to add an endpoint and it should produce
`Task<IActionResult>`, a `BaseResponse<T>`, the right `api/<module>/...` route, an
`OrgId` filter, and the `AddScoped` pair in `DIConfiguration.cs`.

## If PowerShell refuses to run

Nothing above needs admin rights or an execution-policy change - it is pasted
commands, not a script file. If your window is locked down anyway, use Option 1
and let Claude run it.

## Updating later

You will be sent a new copy of this file when the standards change. Run it again -
it backs up your old copy rather than deleting it.
